prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals the full 3D layout of a dark living room that is nearly invisible in the RGB strip, separating the floor, ceiling, and left wall from the far back wall roughly 4 to 6 metres ahead. At the bottom-left within arm's reach (under 1 metre), a bright foreground region marks a seated person and couch armrest partly cropped by the frame edge, while two smaller bright shapes at the bottom-centre and bottom-right (around 0.5 to 0.8 metres) show the camera wearer's own knees and feet. Just behind and to the right of the seated person, a medium-bright mass extending from roughly 1.5 to 3.5 metres ahead delineates a coffee table and an adjacent sofa along the left wall, with open floor space to the right. Across the five frames, the layout stays static until frame 5, when the camera wearer turns slightly left and the bright foreground mass at the bottom-left expands rightward as the nearby person shifts. The map is unreliable around the emissive TV screen at 4 to 5 metres—which disappears completely into the black background void—and along the blurry, merged boundaries between the nearby person, couch, and coffee table.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only a single light-blue mask labelled 'tv' in the upper-left-of-centre region, roughly 4 to 5 metres in front of the camera wearer and about 2 metres beyond the mid-ground coffee table. Across frames 1 to 4 the TV mask stays fixed in position, then shifts slightly rightward in the image in frame 5 as the camera wearer rotates slightly to the left. While this map cleanly localizes the distant television screen that is completely invisible in the depth and pose maps, it provides no other spatial layout or occlusion relationships. It is highly unreliable in the dark environment, failing to segment the person seated within arm's reach at the bottom-left (under 1 metre), the camera wearer's legs at the bottom edge, the coffee table 1.5 to 3 metres ahead, the couches, or the smaller glowing screen just below and to the right of the TV.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, detecting neither body skeletons nor hand keypoints anywhere in the scene. From the RGB and depth strips, at least one person is seated within arm's reach (under 1 metre) at the bottom-left, heavily cropped by the lower-left frame edge and facing forward toward the distant TV rather than looking at the camera wearer, while the camera wearer's own lower legs appear at the bottom-right (under 0.8 metres). Because no skeletons are rendered, the pose map adds nothing that is hard to see in the RGB strip and cannot track the nearby person's slight lean in frame 5 or show what is within anyone's hand reach. The map is entirely unreliable here because extreme low light and severe lower-edge truncation cause a total detection failure.
